content.title: Is an online degree valid in India? How to check a program's UGC-DEB entitlement (2026-27)
content.excerpt: An online degree is valid when UGC-DEB has entitled that exact program for your session. Here is what that means, where the official lists are, and what we found for MUJ, SMU and Amity Online in 2026-27.

body.text: Short answer: an online degree is valid when the UGC Distance Education Bureau (UGC-DEB) has entitled the university to offer that exact program online for the session you join. Entitlement is granted per program and per academic session, so check the program, not just the university.
What the rules say

Online programs are governed by the UGC (Open and Distance Learning Programmes and Online Programmes) Regulations, 2020. UGC-DEB publishes the year-wise list of institutions recognised or entitled to offer programs in online mode at deb.ugc.ac.in. A degree from an entitled online program is treated the same as an on-campus degree under those regulations.
The 2026-27 lists

For the August 2026 session, UGC-DEB published two PDF lists for online programs: institutions entitled to offer online programmes, and a shorter list of institutions recognised to offer them, which also prints a period of recognition. Both are linked from the Recognition section of deb.ugc.ac.in.
What we found for MUJ, SMU and Amity Online

We checked all 30 programs in our catalog against both lists on 5 October 2026. MUJ's nine programs appear on the entitled list under Manipal University, Rajasthan (S.No. 74), and SMU's nine under Sikkim Manipal University, Sikkim (S.No. 80).

Amity Online's programs are printed under two institutions: Amity University Rajasthan and Amity University Uttar Pradesh. Five appear only under Amity University Uttar Pradesh, and for three of those the recognised list prints the recognition as valid up to January 2027. Ask Amity which institution awards your program and what that period means for your batch.
Our recognition check shows each program's published result, with the name exactly as printed, the source and the date we checked it.
Before you enrol

From academic year 2024-25, Indian learners need a DEB-ID to enrol in an online or distance program. You create it on the UGC-DEB portal with your Academic Bank of Credits (ABC) ID. UGC introduced it so that learners enrol only in recognised institutions.

content.title: ABC ID and DEB-ID: what you need before an online degree admission
content.excerpt: From 2024-25, Indian learners need a DEB-ID, created with an ABC ID, to enrol in an online or distance program. Here is what each ID is and the order to create them.

body.text: Short answer: create your Academic Bank of Credits (ABC) ID first, then use it to create a DEB-ID on the UGC-DEB portal, and give that DEB-ID to the university when you apply. You cannot enrol in an online or distance program without a valid DEB-ID.
What the DEB-ID is

UGC-DEB describes the DEB-ID as a unique ID that a learner must create before taking admission in an open and distance learning (ODL) or online program. Its purpose is to make sure learners enrol only in programs of institutions recognised by UGC.
Who needs one

UGC's public notice of 19 August 2024 made the DEB-ID a requirement for every student, except foreign learners, enrolling in ODL or online programs from academic year 2024-25 onwards. The notice says the mechanism for foreign learners is yet to be implemented.
The order to follow
1. Create your ABC ID. UGC-DEB says you can create it through your DigiLocker account.
2. Create your DEB-ID by registering on the UGC-DEB portal (deb.ugc.ac.in) with your ABC ID. A DEB-ID cannot be created without an ABC ID.
3. Choose a university that UGC-DEB recognises, select your program and check that the program is on the list for your session.
4. Complete the admission on the university's portal using your DEB-ID.
How long it lasts

Once created, the DEB-ID stays valid for your lifelong ODL and online learning, so you do not need a new one for a later program. UGC-DEB's FAQ adds that you can be admitted to two academic programs at the same time, in line with UGC's regulations.
Keep your ABC ID and DEB-ID with your admission documents. If you are applying as a foreign learner, ask the university how it handles enrolment while the foreign-learner mechanism is pending.

basedOn.title: NAAC, UGC-DEB, and AICTE: what do these approvals actually mean?
basedOn.excerpt: Three different approvals, three different things they actually certify — with real examples of where they do and don't apply.

body.text: These three approvals are often quoted together as if they're one signal — they're not. Each certifies something different, and a program can hold one without the others.
UGC-DEB entitlement: the one that matters most for validity
This is the specific government approval that makes an online degree valid for that program, at that university, for that academic year. It's checked against a published list, not just claimed.
NAAC: institutional quality, not per-program

NAAC grades the university as a whole, not any specific program. It's a real quality signal, but it doesn't substitute for program-specific UGC-DEB entitlement — and large universities can have multiple separately-graded legal entities, so the grade you see quoted may not be the exact entity granting your specific degree.
AICTE: only relevant to certain technical/management programs
AICTE approval matters for programs like MBA and MCA. It's not relevant to categories like BCA or BBA, which aren't AICTE-regulated at all — so don't expect (or require) it there.
Unnati Vidya tip: when comparing programs, ask which specific approval applies to your exact program, not just whether the university "has approvals" in general.

faqs: Are NAAC, UGC-DEB, and AICTE the same kind of approval?

No — each certifies something different, and a program can hold one without the others. UGC-DEB entitlement is program-and-year-specific; NAAC grades the whole institution; AICTE only applies to certain technical/management programs.
Does a good NAAC grade mean my specific online program is UGC approved?

No — NAAC grades the university as a whole, not any specific program, and doesn't substitute for program-specific UGC-DEB entitlement. Large universities can also have multiple separately-graded legal entities.
Do all online degrees need AICTE approval?
No — AICTE only matters for programs like MBA and MCA. It's not relevant to categories like BCA or BBA, which aren't AICTE-regulated at all.

content.title: NAAC, NIRF, UGC-DEB, AICTE, AIU and WES: what each one means
content.excerpt: These names are often quoted together as if they were one signal. Each covers something different, and only one decides whether a specific online program is entitled.

body.text: These names are often quoted together, but each covers something different. For an online degree, the one that decides whether your specific program is entitled is UGC-DEB.
UGC-DEB: the program's entitlement

UGC-DEB publishes the year-wise lists of institutions entitled or recognised to offer online programs, and the programs under each. It is program-specific and session-specific: a university can be entitled for one program and not another.
NAAC: the institution's accreditation

NAAC accredits the university as a whole, not a specific program. UGC-DEB's 2025-26 entitlement letter ties entitlement to conditions that include NAAC and NIRF, so it matters, but a NAAC grade is not proof that your program is entitled.
NIRF: a national ranking of institutions

NIRF is the Ministry of Education's annual ranking framework. It ranks institutions, not their online programs or mode of delivery, and a large university may have more than one legal entity with different results.
AICTE: technical and management education

AICTE regulates technical and management education. Whether AICTE approval applies to a particular online program depends on the program and AICTE's current rules, so check the program page and ask the university to confirm.
AIU: equivalence of qualifications from outside India

The Association of Indian Universities issues equivalence certificates for qualifications earned outside India. A university can ask for one when your previous degree is from a foreign university; MUJ's admission manual, for example, asks for an AIU equivalence certificate in that case.
WES: credential evaluation abroad
World Education Services evaluates qualifications for people applying to study or work abroad. It is not an Indian approval; see our WES guide for what it involves.
Unnati Vidya tip: when comparing programs, ask which approval applies to your exact program, not whether the university "has approvals" in general.

faqs: Are NAAC, NIRF, UGC-DEB and AICTE the same kind of approval?
No. UGC-DEB entitlement is per program and per session; NAAC accredits the whole institution; NIRF ranks institutions; AICTE regulates technical and management education.
Does a good NAAC grade or NIRF rank mean my online program is entitled?
No. Both describe the institution. Check your program on the UGC-DEB list for your session.
Does my online program need AICTE approval?
It depends on the program and AICTE's current rules. Check the program page and ask the university to confirm.
When would I need an AIU equivalence certificate?
When your previous qualification is from outside India and the university asks for it.

body.text: Short answer: Manipal University Jaipur (MUJ), Sikkim Manipal University (SMU) and Amity University Online each offer a two-year online MBA. They differ most in listed tuition, minimum marks and how specializations are chosen. Check each program's UGC-DEB entitlement for your session before anything else.
Fees for the new batch

Listed on the official program pages on 12 October 2026, before any promotional discount: MUJ ₹1,84,000 (four semester payments of ₹46,000), SMU ₹1,20,000 (four of ₹30,000) and Amity ₹2,25,000 (four semester payments of ₹56,300). MUJ and SMU also list a non-refundable application fee of ₹500.
These are Indian-applicant amounts. NRI and international fees are separate schedules in US dollars; see each course page or the total cost planner.
Who can apply

MUJ asks for a 10+2+3 bachelor's degree with at least 50% marks in aggregate (45% for reserved categories). SMU accepts a 10+2+3, 10+2+4 or 10+3+3 bachelor's degree in any discipline with the same 50% (45%) minimum. Amity asks for graduation in any discipline with at least 40%, and an admission test below 40%.
None of the three lists an entrance exam or work experience as a requirement on its current page. MUJ lists a CAT, GMAT or MAT score and a work-experience certificate as optional documents.
How specializations work

MUJ offers 13 electives, such as Finance, Analytics and Data Science, BFSI and Digital Marketing, and in the third semester you choose one for a super specialization or two for a dual specialization. SMU's MBA is a dual specialization: you pick two of Marketing, Finance, Human Resources, Systems, Operations & Supply Chain Management and Healthcare. Amity lists options including a dual specialization, General Management, Business Analytics, Data Science, Digital Marketing Management, International Finance, and Hospital and Healthcare Management.
Recognition

All three MBAs appeared on the UGC-DEB list of institutions entitled to offer online programmes for 2026-27 when we checked on 5 October 2026: MUJ and SMU under their own names, and Amity's MBA under both Amity University Rajasthan and Amity University Uttar Pradesh. Ask Amity which institution awards your degree.
How to choose

Settle four things in order: whether the program is entitled for your session, whether you meet the marks requirement comfortably, which specialization fits the role you want, and the full amount you will pay, including how payments are spaced. The cheapest option is not automatically the right one, and the most expensive is not automatically better.

content.title: No-cost EMI for an online degree: how it works and what to check
content.excerpt: No-cost EMI spreads a degree fee into monthly payments, but it is still a loan. Here is what the RBI says about zero percent schemes, and what to check before you sign.

body.text: Short answer: a no-cost EMI is a loan. A lender pays the fee and you repay it in monthly instalments that are meant to add up to the fee. Before you sign, ask the lender for its Key Facts Statement and check the total you will repay, including any processing fee.
It is still a loan

With a no-cost EMI, a bank or finance company lends you the fee and you repay that lender each month. Whether you are approved, and on what terms, is the lender's decision, not the university's. The loan is a separate contract from your admission.
What the RBI has said about zero percent schemes

In a circular to banks dated 17 September 2013, the Reserve Bank of India said that in zero percent EMI schemes on credit card outstandings, "the interest element is often camouflaged and passed on to customer in the form of processing fee". It added that "the very concept of zero percent interest is non-existent". So look at the charges, not the label.
Ask for the Key Facts Statement

For new retail and MSME term loans sanctioned on or after 1 October 2024, banks and NBFCs must give you a Key Facts Statement (KFS) before you sign. It includes the annual percentage rate (APR), which covers the interest rate and all other charges the lender levies, and a repayment schedule for the whole loan.

A fee or charge that is not in the KFS cannot be charged later without your explicit consent. For loans of seven days or more, the KFS stays valid for at least three working days, so you have time to read and compare it. The lender asks you to confirm that you have understood it.
The KFS rules do not cover credit card receivables. If the EMI runs on your credit card, ask the card issuer for every charge in writing before you choose it.
What to check before you sign
1. The total you will repay. Add up every instalment and any processing fee, and compare it with the fee the university lists for your applicant category.
2. The APR on the KFS. If it is not zero, ask the lender which charges make it up.
3. Who the lender is, and how and when you pay each month.
4. When the first instalment is due, compared with the university's semester payment dates.
5. Charges for a late payment or for closing the loan early.
6. What happens if you leave the program. The university's refund policy and your loan are separate, so ask both whether a refund closes the loan.
EMI at MUJ, SMU and Amity

Every university we list offers no-cost EMI. The monthly amount on our course pages is the listed tuition divided by the program's months, as a guide. The lender confirms your actual instalment and terms.
No-cost EMI changes how you pay, not what the program costs. Compare programs on the listed fee and what you get first, then decide how to pay.

faqs: Is no-cost EMI really free?

Not always. The RBI has said that the concept of zero percent interest is non-existent, and that interest can be passed on as a processing fee. Check the total you will repay and the APR on the lender's Key Facts Statement.
What is a Key Facts Statement?

A standard summary that banks and NBFCs must give before a new retail or MSME term loan sanctioned on or after 1 October 2024. It shows the APR, which includes the interest rate and all other charges the lender levies, and the repayment schedule.
Is the EMI amount on Unnati Vidya the amount I will pay?
It is a guide: the listed tuition divided by the program's months. The lender confirms your actual instalment, charges and schedule.
What happens to my EMI if I leave the program?
Your loan is a separate contract with the lender, and refunds follow the university's own policy. Ask both, before you sign, whether a refund closes the loan.

content.title: Online, distance or regular: what each mode means for your degree
content.excerpt: UGC defines three ways to study for a degree: regular, open and distance learning, and online. Here is how they differ in teaching, exams and recognition, and how to check which one you are joining.

body.text: Short answer: all three can lead to an equivalent degree. Under UGC's 2020 regulations, a degree earned in open and distance learning (ODL) or online mode from an institution recognised under those regulations is treated as equivalent to the same degree in regular (conventional) mode. What differs is how you are taught and examined, and the mode the university must be recognised for.
How UGC defines the three modes
Regular (conventional) mode: learning through "face to face interaction between the teacher and learner in regular class room environment", which can be supplemented with online instruction.

Open and distance learning (ODL): learning through "a variety of media, including print, electronic, online and occasional interactive face-to-face meetings" with learners, or through learner support services.
Online mode: learning through the internet and e-learning materials, with "full-fledged programme delivery through the internet".
How you are assessed

For both ODL and online programs, continuous assessment during the semester counts for at most 30% of the marks and the end-semester exam for at least 70%. To sit the end-semester exam, an online learner needs at least 75% participation in the program's online activities, and an ODL learner needs 75% attendance in its personal contact sessions.

ODL end-semester exams are proctored in examination centres within the university's territorial jurisdiction. Online programs can hold exams as technology-enabled online tests with security arrangements, or as proctored exams, and the territorial restriction does not apply to online learning.
Recognition is for a mode, a program and a session

The regulations set separate conditions for offering ODL and online programs, and UGC-DEB publishes separate lists for each, year by year. Check that your program is listed in the mode you are joining, for your session.
The programs we list at MUJ, SMU and Amity Online are offered in online mode. On 5 October 2026 we found all 30 on UGC-DEB's 2026-27 list of institutions entitled to offer online programmes.
A "UGC approved" badge on a program page is not enough on its own. Check the mode and the session on deb.ugc.ac.in, or use our recognition check.
Choosing between them

Regular mode suits you if you can attend classes in person. Online and ODL let you study around work or from a distance: an online program is delivered entirely over the internet, while ODL can also use printed material and occasional face-to-face sessions. Whichever you choose, the equivalence applies only if the institution is recognised for that mode and program.

body.text: Short answer: World Education Services (WES) evaluates your own credentials and reports how they compare with qualifications in the country you are applying to. You request the evaluation; your university sends your academic records to WES.
Who asks for a WES evaluation

Canada's immigration department (IRCC) lists WES as one of five organizations designated to issue educational credential assessments (ECAs) for Express Entry. If you studied outside Canada, you need an ECA to qualify as a principal applicant under the Federal Skilled Workers Program or to earn points for education obtained abroad, and the ECA must be less than five years old when you complete your profile and when you apply.
Employers, universities and licensing bodies elsewhere may ask for WES or for another evaluator. Check which evaluations the organization you are applying to accepts.
What WES asks for from Indian degrees

WES accepts consolidated transcripts or yearly mark sheets, provided they are issued by the degree-granting institution and sent in a sealed envelope. The institution sends them directly to WES; if it won't, WES says you may be able to send the sealed envelope yourself. Institutions with a digital partnership can send records electronically, and you can also upload documents to an NSDC digital wallet, which verifies and passes them to WES.

Include a copy of your degree or provisional certificate and the mark sheets for all years. For most master's degrees, WES also needs your bachelor's documents. Your WES account's required-documents list is the final word for your case.
If your degree was earned online

WES's India requirements page doesn't say anything specific about online or distance degrees. Ask your university how it issues records for online programs, and check your WES account's required documents before you send anything. In India, UGC's 2020 regulations treat an online degree from a recognised institution as equivalent to the regular degree; how another country evaluates it is decided by that country's evaluator.
A university page that calls its degrees "WES recognised" is describing them in its own words. What counts for your application is your own WES evaluation report.

Before you enrol, ask: which sessions are live and when, whether recordings are available, how participation is counted, and how much time the program expects each week.
